ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, govern reporting entities, including covered financial institutions and money services businesses; an ordinary auto-parts retailer is not generally a reporting entity solely by reason of retail sales. Alberta ULCs are governed principally by the Companies Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. C-21. Alberta's registry and record-keeping requirements must be confirmed for the chosen legal form; federal CBCA significant-control register provisions do not automatically apply to an Alberta-incorporated entity. Alberta does not operate a generally public beneficial-ownership register for Alberta ULCs. Canadian sanctions obligations include the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, and applicable regulations, the United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or equivalent formation record for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or other competent corporate authority in the entity's jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is party to the Apostille Convention and the document is eligible; otherwise consular legalization, subject to Canadian acceptance requirements

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or current registry extract for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or other competent corporate authority in the entity's jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if eligible; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or power of attorney authorizing Alberta incorporation and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder, executed by its authorized officers; notarization or witnessing as required by the receiving registry or service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for notarized public instrument where available; otherwise consular legalization where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or government-issued identity document and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority and regulated address-document issuer in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy, notarization, apostille, or consular legalization only where required by the receiving institution; there is no universal Alberta incorporation requirement for apostilled identity documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ownership chart and beneficial-owner declaration identifying natural persons and control arrangements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Prepared and certified by the applicant or its authorized representative, supported by underlying corporate records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization or legalization only if required by the registry, financial institution, or professional intermediary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding and periodically thereafter, identify direct and indirect natural-person ownership and control, verify identity and address, screen relevant persons and counterparties against applicable Canadian sanctions lists and UN Security Council measures, and document risk-based screening against OFAC lists where relevant to U.S. nexus, payment rails, counterparties, or bank policy. PEP and head-of-international-organization screening and enhanced measures are legally required for applicable Canadian PCMLTFA reporting entities; they are not a universal statutory requirement for an ordinary auto-parts retailer, but banks, payment processors, and other regulated intermediaries commonly require risk-based screening. Record match disposition, source, date, and escalation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry services, accessed through an authorized Alberta registry agent; NUANS name search and reservation services are used for proposed corporate names
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A proposed Alberta corporate name must comply with the Companies Act and applicable regulations and be distinguishable from existing names and trademarks. English and French forms may be used; non-Latin characters and transliterations should be confirmed with the registry agent. A numbered company may be used where permitted. A name search is not trademark clearance and does not establish freedom to use a name nationally.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying a connection with the Crown, government, or a government department without required consent
Bank, trust, insurance, university, professional, or other regulated-sector terms requiring statutory approval or consent
Words that are obscene, misleading, or contrary to public policy
Names identical or deceptively similar to existing corporate names, business names, or protected marks
Terms suggesting a regulated financial, charitable, or professional status that the entity does not possess
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Confirm the rejection reason and obtain the registry decision or deficiency notice; revise the proposed name or submit documentary evidence supporting distinctiveness or required consent; refile through an authorized Alberta registry agent and pay applicable fees. If the refusal is legally reviewable, request reconsideration or pursue the applicable statutory court or administrative remedy within the prescribed time. Alberta name reservations are generally time-limited; confirm the effective expiry on the reservation record and do not assume an extension is available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An Alberta registered office and records address must satisfy the applicable Companies Act requirements and be in Alberta. A commercial registered-office or records-office provider may be usable if it meets those requirements and can reliably receive and forward service and official notices. A mailbox-only address is inadequate. A virtual office does not establish operational substance, resolve banking or payment-processor diligence, or satisfy any separate licensing, consumer-protection, tax, or employment requirements. An online auto-parts retailer generally has no sector-specific physical-premises licence solely because it sells replacement parts, but inventory and fulfillment arrangements must be accurately represented.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable public statistic quantifies unannounced inspections for this activity. Routine corporate registry inspections are not generally expected; tax, consumer-protection, occupational health and safety, fire, municipal, or other inspections may occur on a risk-based or complaint basis. Do not represent the likelihood as a quantified percentage.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9 (ABCA), ss. 14-15 (incorporation and unlimited liability corporation designation), s. 132 (registered office), s. 129 (first directors), s. 26 (consideration for shares), and the General Regulation under the ABCA; ULC shareholder liability for corporate debts applies under s. 15(5)-(8), including a two-year tail after transfer of shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), containing an express statement that the corporation is an unlimited liability corporation (ULC) under ABCA s. 15
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or trust account requirement for an Alberta ULC; shares may be issued for money, property or past services, and at least one shareholder is required; the corporation's statement of capital is as set out in the Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, THAT the shares subscribed by the incorporating shareholders be and are hereby allotted from the authorized capital of the Corporation, and share certificates shall be issued upon payment of full consideration.
RESOLVED, THAT the registered office of the Corporation be established at the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, and such address shall be maintained as a continuous Alberta business address.
RESOLVED, THAT the model by-laws of the Corporation be adopted, and Bylaw No. 1 shall become effective immediately.
RESOLVED, THAT the following officers be and are hereby appointed: President, Secretary, Treasurer, and Managing Director, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board.
RESOLVED, THAT the Corporation may open accounts, retain advisers, and do all things to perfect corporate governance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry - Name Reservation Unit, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction; NUANS report procured through an authorized NUANS search house
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Decide whether to use a distinctive corporate name or a numbered company. For a branded auto-parts e-commerce operation, procure a NUANS corporate name search report through an approved provider, verify that the proposed name and up to two alternatives are distinguishable from existing trademarks and corporate names, and file a name reservation request with the Corporate Registry. The reservation is valid for 90 days and may be renewed once. If a numbered company is preferred, no NUANS report is required.
required_dossiers: NUANS report from an authorized provider
Name reservation request with up to three proposed names
Incorporator contact details and any required trademark disclaimer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusing or non-distinctive, file a perfected reservation with amended names; if the registry denies on public policy grounds, request a written refusal and internal review, or apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles of Incorporation and Governance Pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and named first directors of the ULC; prescribed Alberta corporate forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation expressly stating that the corporation is an unlimited liability corporation under ABCA s. 15. Include the proposed corporate name, the street address of the registered office in Alberta, the class and maximum number of shares, any restrictions on share transfers, and the number of first directors. Draft the initial by-laws, share subscription agreements, and consents to act as director. No notarization is required for the domestic filing; if foreign incorporators are used, arrange a notarized and apostilled corporate resolution appointing the Alberta incorporator and submitted identity documents.
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation (draft)
Consent to act as first director for each director
Initial by-laws or model by-laws election
Registered office and records address consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registry staff recommend changes to restrictive provisions or capital structure, amend and resubmit the articles; a filing date may be preserved where corrections are made within the registry inquiry period; if the Registrar refuses filing, seek relief from the Court of King's Bench under ABCA s. 263.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Payment of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry (Registry Connect online portal or accredited filing service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Articles of Incorporation and submit them online through Registry Connect or an accredited filing service. Pay the statutory incorporation fee by approved credit card or registered account (CAD 275 online; CAD 300 paper filing), and obtain an electronic acknowledgment of receipt containing the Corporate Access Number.
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation (executed)
Statutory filing fee payment authorization
Service provider filing authorization where an agent is engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for incomplete payment or defective form, correct the portal errors and resubmit; where a Notice of Intention to Refuse is issued, respond within the stated period with written submissions, or re-file a perfected set of articles preserving priority if the error is purely formal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Corporate Access Number and CRA Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry; Canada Revenue Agency (automatic data exchange)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation showing the statutory incorporation date and Corporate Access Number. The Alberta Corporate Registry automatically transmits incorporation data to the Canada Revenue Agency, which assigns the 9-digit Business Number. Verify the Business Number in CRA's Business Registration Online portal and confirm that the legal name and registered office address are accurate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by the Registrar)
Corporate Access Number
CRA Business Number confirmation record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Number is not issued within five business days, apply to CRA separately in writing or online using the certificate number and legal name; if the registered office entry is inaccurate, file Form 2 - Notice of Registered Office to correct the registry record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Organizational Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Alberta ULC (internal statutory governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Call the organizational meeting of the first directors or execute a written consent resolution. Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution covering share allotment and subscription, adoption of the registered office, ratification of by-laws, and appointment of the President, Secretary, Treasurer, and Managing Director. Issue share certificates against consideration, approve a banking resolution, and appoint external legal counsel and accountants.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Share subscription, allotment, and certificate records
Officer appointment and acceptance forms
Bank resolution and incumbency certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Quorum or notice defects are cured by an unanimous written consent resolution executed by all directors; an omitted appointment is remedied by a supplemental board resolution filed in the minute book, and any resulting change in directors is filed with the Registry on Form 3 - Notice of Directors within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Notice of Directors and Registered Office Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the initial directors named in Form 1 are reflected in the Registry's public record. File Form 3 - Notice of Directors for any changes and Form 2 - Notice of Registered Office for any change occurring after incorporation. Maintain current registry records to support e-commerce vendor contracts, banking, and sales tax registration.
required_dossiers: Form 3 - Notice of Directors (executed)
Form 2 - Notice of Registered Office (if applicable)
Consent to act as director for each new director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late changes are filed with the applicable late-filing fee; registrable errors are cured by an amended notice within the correction period and, if necessary, by a written correction request to the Registrar referencing the Certificate of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Records Office, Corporate Minute Book, and Physical Address Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary and directors; municipal business licensing authority for physical address verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the Alberta registered records office holding the corporate minute book, securities register, register of directors, articles, by-laws, and shareholder registers. Ensure the registered office street address is a bona fide Alberta address where service of process can be effected during business hours. Register the operational warehouse address with the municipal business licensing authority in connection with the municipal business licence application.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book and statutory registers
Registered office and records address documents
Municipal business address registration or business licence application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office becomes unusable or non-compliant, file a Notice of Change of Registered Office immediately and pay the administrative filing fee; if the records address is queried, produce the Certificate of Incorporation and confirm the commercial address with the Registry within the inquiry window to avoid administrative dissolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta municipal business licensing authority of the location of the warehouse (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licence Office or City of Edmonton Business Licensing); provincial safety oversight by Safety Codes Council and Alberta Labour (Occupational Health and Safety Division); environmental oversight by Alberta Environment and Protected Areas
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (General Retail / Warehouse and Distribution) under the Municipal Government Act, RSA 2000, c. M-26; no Alberta provincial trade licence is prescribed for ISIC 4791 online automotive parts retail, but the physical warehouse premises require a municipal business licence and Safety Codes Act occupancy permits.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEP), Environmental Assessment and Approvals Program; federal coordination with Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) where an Impact Assessment Act designation is triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA - online retail of pre-manufactured automotive parts with warehousing is not a listed mandatory activity under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA); an EPEA registration may become mandatory only if on-site hazardous waste storage, solvent degreasing, or vehicle maintenance operations exceed regulatory thresholds; no federal Impact Assessment Act designation is anticipated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharge to municipal sanitary sewer only, meeting the applicable municipal Sewer Use Bylaw limits (typical parameters include pH 6.0-9.0, total suspended solids not exceeding 350 mg/L, and oil and grease not exceeding 100 mg/L). Emissions: VOC usage from parts cleaning solvents must remain below the EPEA registration threshold and comply with Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 solvent degreasing regulations; particulate and combustion emissions from any heating equipment must meet provincial ambient air quality objectives. Waste: spent oil, lead-acid batteries, antifreeze, and aerosol remnants are hazardous wastes under the Alberta Waste Control Regulation (AR 192/1996), requiring manifests, approved transporters, and a maximum accumulation time of 90 days on site unless an EPEA registration for hazardous waste storage is obtained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and life safety inspection certificate from the municipal fire authority under the Alberta Fire Code and the Safety Codes Act, RSA 2000, c. S-1, covering the warehouse occupancy, fire separations, exits, and storage of combustible materials; municipal building occupancy permit confirming structural load and electrical safety compliance; mandatory Workers' Compensation Board (WCB-Alberta) employer account registration; workplace hazard assessment, first-aid kit, and health and safety program per the Alberta OHS Act and OHS Code 2009; and, where materials-handling equipment is used, equipment inspection and operator certification records must be maintained.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada. Single federal tax authority for corporate income tax, GST/HST, and Alberta's provincial corporate income tax (which the CRA administers under a collection agreement with Alberta; Alberta levies no provincial sales tax). Operational portal: CRA My Business Account at canada.ca/cra-my-business-account; GST/HST NETFILE; corporate T2 e-file mandate applies. Ancillary registry: Alberta Corporate Registry for ULC incorporation, extra-provincial registration, and annual registry returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the ULC in Alberta (or import a BC/other provincial ULC into Alberta) through the Alberta Corporate Registry; the Business Number (BN) of 9 digits is automatically assigned by the CRA via integrated registration. Step 2 — Activate the GST/HST program account (RM prefix) online through My Business Account or by filing Form RC1A; the CRA issues the 15-character GST/HST registration number. Step 3 — For a ULC incorporated outside Alberta, file for extra-provincial registration with the Alberta Corporate Registry, obtain the Alberta Corporate Access/registry file number, and file the Alberta annual return. Step 4 — Register with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for an exporter account (for U.S./foreign export clearance and B13A declarations). Step 5 — File the T2 corporate income tax return (mandatory e-file) covering both federal Part I tax and Alberta corporate income tax (Alberta schedules embedded in T2); keep trade name, registered office, and directors updated with both the CRA and Alberta Registry. Step 6 — For U.S.-parented ULCs, the U.S. owner may concurrently file IRS Form 8832 (check-the-box) and obtain a U.S. EIN, but Canadian registration remains that of a separate taxable corporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the ULC is a separate person and a taxable Canadian corporation under Income Tax Act (ITA) s. 248(1); it is not fiscally transparent in Canada. Taxed at federal Part I general rate of 15% and Alberta corporate income tax of 8% (23% combined) on worldwide income unless a treaty/foreign tax credit applies; the small-business rate (9% federal + 2% Alberta on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income) is available only if the ULC is a Canadian-controlled private corporation. For GST/HST, the ULC is a separate registrant person. 'Pass_Through_Eligible' applies solely on the U.S. federal tax side under check-the-box, creating hybrid entity exposure that Canada's hybrid mismatch rules seek to neutralize. Dividends paid to non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax (25% statutory rate, reduced to 5% for a U.S.-resident corporate shareholder holding 10% or more of voting shares under the Canada-U.S. tax treaty). Alberta is a non-participating province: no PST, no sub-provincial VAT, but Alberta corporate income tax is a separate provincial levy administered by the CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (i) U.S. check-the-box election (IRS Form 8832) to treat the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership — the defining election for a ULC owned by U.S. residents; in Canada the entity remains taxable at the entity level. (ii) Hybrid mismatch documentation and remedial timing elections under Canada's BEPS Action 2 rules, which may deny the ULC's deduction for payments to a fiscal-transparent U.S. owner (deduction-without-inclusion) unless the U.S. owner includes the corresponding income; a discretionary CRA interpretive ruling can be requested. (iii) GST/HST election under s. 156 of the Excise Tax Act (Form GST25) to leave GST uncharged on taxable supplies of auto parts between the ULC and closely related registered corporations. (iv) Quick Method of accounting election (Form GST74) where annual global taxable supplies do not exceed CAD 400,000, allowing simplified net-tax remittance for the e-commerce retail arm. (v) Fiscal-period election to adopt any 12-month fiscal year (non-calendar permitted) for T2 purposes. (vi) Election to file consolidated? Not available; Alberta income tax is fully harmonized into the federal T2 return with no separate provincial election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) — a VAT-type consumption tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act. Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST because it is a non-participating province with no provincial sales tax; deliveries to HST provinces require the destination province's HST rate (e.g., 13% in Ontario, 15% in Nova Scotia).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the 'small supplier' threshold under ETA s. 148(1): GST/HST registration becomes mandatory when global taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters. Once registered, the Alberta ULC must charge 5% GST on Alberta-destination sales and the applicable HST rate for goods delivered into participating provinces; U.S./foreign export sales are zero-rated. Non-resident vendor deemed-supplier rules (July 1, 2021 on) do not apply because the ULC is a Canadian resident supplier.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory government stamping, and no continuous transaction controls (CTC) for e-invoicing as of 2025; voluntary PEPPOL/EDI standards are accepted. Mandatory electronic filing applies to GST/HST returns for registrants with annual global supplies exceeding CAD 1,500,000 (filed via GST/HST NETFILE or CRA XML EDI) and to T2 corporate returns. The CRA requires retention of all electronic invoices and source documents (Stripe/PayPal settlement data, courier manifests) for six years in an auditable format. CBSA operates the Canadian Export Reporting System for export declarations, but this is a customs, not GST, clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. To claim 0% GST on automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories exported from the Alberta warehouse: (i) the ULC must be a GST/HST registrant; (ii) the supply must be by way of sale; (iii) the goods must be exported as soon as is reasonable after the supply, whether by the supplier or by the non-resident purchaser; and (iv) delivery/possession must be transferred to a destination outside Canada and the consignee must be non-resident. Exports to the U.S. satisfy these criteria when the parts are shipped via a common carrier from Alberta to a U.S. address. Related services supplied to non-residents in respect of exported goods (e.g., international freight and handling services provided by the seller) may also be zero-rated. The ULC may claim input tax credits (ITCs) for GST paid on importation of the parts into Canada where support by CBSA customs documents if the corresponding export is properly zero-rated. Until the goods physically leave Canada, in-transit domestic sales are taxable at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — CBSA Form B13A filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) or the carrier's/customs broker's automated export system; mandatory for goods valued over CAD 2,000 or controlled goods (e.g., airbags classified as controlled), with the B13A identifier referenced on the commercial invoice
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier evidencing dispatch from Canada and the foreign (typically U.S.) destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank FX credit confirmation (SWIFT MT103) or corporate bank statement showing the foreign buyer's proceeds received into the ULC's Canadian bank account
Commercial invoice, packing list, purchase order, and the ULC's shipping manifest confirming the overseas consignee
Platform settlement reports from Stripe/PayPal tying the payment ledger to the specific export order and foreign destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess within the normal four-year period under ETA s. 298, which is unlimited where there is misrepresentation, neglect, carelessness, or fraud. If the contemporaneous export documents are deficient, the zero-rating is reversed and the ULC is assessed for uncollected GST at 5% (plus HST rate differentials for deliveries to participating provinces), with daily compound interest. The gross-negligence penalty under ETA s. 285.1 is the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the tax; wilful evasion under ETA s. 327 attracts a civil penalty of 50%-200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment. False or omitted export declarations also expose the ULC to Customs Act penalties and CBSA compliance enforcement. On the income side, failure to collect evidence of repatriation within the 180-day benchmark (no rule per se in the ETA, but the 180-day period is the standard CRA exchange-of-information/administrative expectation for export substantiation) may lead to ITA s. 247 transfer-pricing recharacterization of unrepatriated intercompany receivables and adjustment to the export price. The correlative ITC position on imported parts is clawed back when the corresponding outward supply is reclassified as taxable in Canada.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada / Banque du Canada is the monetary authority; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions regulates banks; FINTRAC administers AML/EFT transaction reporting. Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange control administration and no exchange-control approval body for current or capital account transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility under IMF Article VIII for both current and capital account; the Canadian dollar is a freely floating currency. No prior government approval is required for capital injections, loan repayments, dividend distributions, profit remittances, or liquidation proceeds. The only material remittance friction is Canadian non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, generally 25% unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty, and standard bank source-of-funds verification; this is not an FX-control restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose mandatory surrender, conversion ratios, or statutory repatriation timelines for export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency; however, for Canadian income tax purposes they must be expressed in Canadian dollars using Bank of Canada exchange rates. Financial institutions must report international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC and retain supporting records for five years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account and LC collateral account for trade finance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-low as a primary treasury rail; acceptable as a secondary settlement rail. Foreign EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, or Revolut Business may be used for low-value FX conversion and vendor disbursements, but must be FINTRAC-registered as money services businesses to operate in Canada. They are not chartered banks, offer no CDIC deposit insurance, and cannot support letters of credit, Canadian payroll, tax payments, or a full relationship banking facility. The ULC should maintain its primary operating account at a Schedule I bank and use Stripe/PayPal for customer collection and EMIs only for wallet-style cross-border payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Federal PCMLTFA does not require a physical branch interview; remote account opening is legally permissible if the bank performs compliant identity verification. In practice, Schedule I banks allow remote onboarding for a low-risk Alberta ULC with authenticated corporate registry records and video/liveness identity verification. For non-resident UBOs or signatories, banks generally require notarized or consular-certified ID, certified corporate register, and a live video call. Some banks may still require an in-person meeting at an Alberta branch or Canadian consular office for higher-risk non-resident ownership or PEP/sanctions-related hits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity due to Alberta unlimited liability corporation structure and non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized certificate of incumbency, constating documents, articles/amalgamation documents, share register, Alberta corporate registry search, UBO declaration covering all 25% or more owners, director resolutions, passports or government-issued IDs of directors and UBOs, and a bank reference letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding with non-resident directors or UBOs in high-risk or sanctions-listed jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of ID, utility bill with residential address, apostille or consular legalization where required, live video identity verification transcript, independent background-search report, registered-office lease or Alberta legal-address evidence, and source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, small-ticket e-commerce inflows through Stripe and PayPal appearing as treated deposits or laundering patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed PSP merchant agreements, product catalogue, order-invoice-shipping records, PSP settlement reports, refund and chargeback history, customer support logs, website terms and delivery policy, customs and HS classification data for auto parts, and relevant corporate tax filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade payables to overseas auto-aftermarket suppliers in jurisdictions with elevated sanctions or trade-based money-laundering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC dossier, beneficial ownership declaration for supplier, purchase orders, contract for sale, Incoterms declarations, bills of lading, airway bills, customs entry or export declarations, sanctions screening results, and a complete order-to-payment audit trail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the ULC's Alberta bank, with beneficiary legal name, account number, bank/transit/ABA/BIC, and narrative identifying the payment as an equity contribution or shareholder loan. Canada has no prescribed Bank of Canada purpose code, but the payment instruction must state the true economic nature. The bank will apply FINTRAC international EFT reporting at CAD 10,000 or more and will verify source of funds through bank statements, UBO declarations, and corporate authorizations. For shareholder debt, execute a written loan agreement with interest and repayment terms, prepare CRA Form T106 if applicable, and maintain arm's-length transfer-pricing documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For high-value supplier payments use SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer with full invoice and purchase-order references, or, where a letter of credit is required, use documentary LC settlement through a Canadian bank under UCP600. CAD-denominated domestic payments can clear through Lynx, Real-Time Rail, or standard EFT; USD trade payments may be cleared via Fedwire or CHIPS through a USD sub-account at a Schedule I bank. Recurring low-value supplier payouts can use bank batch files, Stripe/PayPal payouts, or a FINTRAC-registered EMI wallet. Maintain a clear audit trail of customs invoices, Incoterms, shipping documents, and FX tickets.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable CAD/USD FX forward with a Schedule I Canadian bank or an eligible foreign bank counterparty
Spot-forward FX swap and tom-next swap for cash-flow timing and trade settlement liquidity
Cross-currency swap on commercial borrowings or intercompany debt, designated under IFRS 9 hedge accounting
Currency call or put options under an ISDA/CSA master agreement for economic hedging of USD receivables or payables
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) only for a restricted non-CAD currency pair, such as USD/CNH, where there is a documented underlying supplier exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (ABCA Annual Corporate Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry - Service Alberta, Edmonton (online or paper filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each annual return-date anniversary (incorporation, amalgamation, or continuation date); the return date remains fixed every year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Placement in registry default; failure to file for two consecutive return dates permits administrative strike-off/dissolution by the Registrar; reinstatement requires all outstanding returns, reinstatement fees, and registry costs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal plus Alberta corporate tax administered by CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - T2 e-filed through a registered E-Filer or CRA My Business Account
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within six months after the end of each fiscal period (e.g., December 31 year-end is due by June 30); Alberta has no separate paper corporate tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid balance at the due date plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months (maximum 17%); aggravated C$2,000-per-month penalty (maximum 12 months) may apply where gross revenue exceeds C$1,000,000 and the return is more than two years late; arrears interest accrues on unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Goods and Services Tax (GST) Return (Alberta has no HST component; GST rate 5%)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST division) - filed online via GST/HST NETFILE or a CRA-approved filing service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers must file and remit within three months after the fiscal period end; where monthly or quarterly filing applies, returns are due within one month after each reporting period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to the greater of C$250 or 1% of the reporting period's net tax; prescribed-rate interest on unremitted net tax; failure to remit collected GST may expose directors to CRA liability and loss of annual-filer eligibility.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Internal statutory registers audit pack (Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Share Transfers, and Minute Book) together with corporate standing certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at the Alberta registered office; available for inspection by the Alberta Corporate Registry and by shareholders under the ABCA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update concurrently with the annual return cycle and at each director or shareholder meeting; registers are not filed with the Registry unless required by notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct Registry fine for record-keeping delay, but ABCA offence provisions may apply for failure to produce or maintain registers; deficiencies impair security-rights perfection, financing, and due diligence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the ABCA, an auditor must be appointed at the annual meeting level, but a non-distributing private ULC may waive independent audit by unanimous written shareholder consent for each fiscal year. There is no Alberta revenue-asset statutory audit threshold; a full audit is unavoidable for distributing or reporting issuers, ULCs with lender or shareholder audit covenants, and ULCs consolidated into a US or other foreign parent requiring attestation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) apply to the stand-alone ULC statutory financial statements; IFRS is required for reporting issuers and may be voluntarily adopted; US GAAP may be used only for the parent group consolidation and not for Alberta statutory book purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not currently require a public annual beneficial-ownership filing for a provincial ULC. The ULC's member register must be updated promptly on every share issuance or transfer, including transfers between Canadian and non-resident members; the Alberta Annual Return confirms only the current directors. If the Alberta ABCA individuals-with-significant-control transparency provisions apply to the ULC, an ISC register must be maintained at the registered office and updated upon each ownership change, but no annual registry submission is made under the present ABCA framework.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (where the new ABCA transparency provisions apply)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 250-800 (USD-equivalent of CAD 330-1,080) per annum for commercial registered office and registered agent services in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 6,000-18,000 per annum for a small or medium online retail ULC full independent audit; USD 3,000-7,000 for an accountant's review engagement where the audit is waived

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate rate (15% federal + 8% Alberta); 11% combined small-business rate (9% federal + 2% Alberta) where the ULC qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for Alberta e-commerce; federal General Rate Reduction applied; small business deduction limited and generally unavailable to ULCs controlled by non-residents; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits at 15–35% on qualifying R&D; 20-year non-capital loss carryforward and 3-year carryback
